content_html:
Intro

AI Avatar is a free app where your VRoid (VRM) avatar cheers you with all its might.🤗 It lives in your VS Code sidebar (reacts to Claude Code /Codex /GitHub Copilot) or browser side panel (reacts to ChatGPT / Claude). Animations and speech bubbles all run without AI too.

This time, I have 3 main topics.

  • AI Avatar Security
  • Voxel Avatar Update
  • AWS Clean Up

Let's check them out together!😆

AI Avatar Security

In Japan, unauthorized access and sensitive data leaks caused by hackers have increased dramatically since September. I heard that personal data records exceeding twice Japan's population have now been leaked. This security situation does not seem to be happening only in Japan but also around the world. It’s quite horrifying. I wonder if this is partly due to the development of AI.

I have been using AI at work and for fun every day for more than a year, and I know how much smarter it has become in a short time. So this time, I decided to add a security support feature called AI Avatar Security to AI Avatar.

I am not a security expert, and I made it to learn about security. But I hope this will be helpful to others too. I also hope it will motivate others to learn more about security incidents.

There are three main features in AI Avatar Security.

  • Security Check
  • AI Review
  • Security News

Security Check

In Security Check, there are two types of checks. A library vulnerability check and a data leakage check. The library vulnerability check uses npm audit to check for the known vulnerabilities. It lets you know which libraries have vulnerabilities. The data leakage check uses Betterleaks (formerly Gitleaks) to detect exposed keys and passwords.

Security is not such a fun thing, but I added avatar animations based on the check results and tried to make it a little more fun and motivating.

NG Animation

If there are any security issues, a virus-like animation is played. It doesn’t mean the app is infected with a virus.🦠 I added the animation to make security checks more fun.

OK Animation

If there are no problems, a shining animation is played. Let’s feel relieved that there are no problems.

AI Review

I added an AI prompt for security checks to help prevent unauthorized access and sensitive data leakage. I also added an option to add tests for them.

Category What AI checks
Unauthorized Access Login and authentication
Unauthorized Access Roles and permissions
Unauthorized Access Data between users and teams
Unauthorized Access Private files and downloads
Sensitive Data Leakage Keys and passwords
Sensitive Data Leakage Private data in responses
Sensitive Data Leakage Logs and error messages
Sensitive Data Leakage Public files and storage

You can scan all eight at once, but scanning just one at a time seemed to provide a deeper analysis.

Security News

I added a security news checker. It uses two sources:

CIS (Center for Internet Security) for software vulnerabilities, and

NCSC (National Cyber Security Centre) for general security advice.

Please check the latest security news and update your security knowledge.

AWS Cleanup

By the way, I was also checking and improving my personal cybersecurity. I finally got off my butt and decided to clean up my AWS account. I was just stopping my services to avoid getting charged and wasn’t deleting them because I knew it would be so hard and take time.

Some of the services couldn’t be deleted all at once, and I needed to delete them one by one by entering their names. So I asked my AI to write code that could delete them all at once using CloudShell. First, I was deleting the services shown in CloudWatch logs, but soon I noticed that this didn’t cover all services. So next, I used Resource Explorer, enabled indexing in all regions, and checked which services I had used were still left. But default settings that didn’t need to be deleted also showed up. So I asked AI to scan and list only the services I had used. I finally deleted all the unnecessary services.

A few days later, I checked Cost Explorer and found that I had been charged a few dollars because deleting the services had triggered Config. I would have deleted the whole account if I had known it would be so hard and that I would even have to pay more.

However, I love using AWS because it is convenient and offers many services, so I would like to keep using it. But from now on, I will try to clean up regularly and avoid accumulating too many resources.

Voxel Avatar Update


Voxel Avatar is an idle game where you can grow a garden and place animals while using VS Code and the Chrome extension. My DEV friend @shubhradev gave me a great idea in my previous post, a winter version. Thank you for your idea! So I added a snow animation this time. It made the voxel world look completely different and fun. The Voxel Avatar feature has grown into one of the core features of AI Avatar, so I would like to update it even more.

How to Use the AI Avatar VS Code Extension Version (Thank you 400+ installs!)

You can download the AI Avatar VS Code extension in two ways.

  • Option 1: Install from VS Code: Extensions button in the left sidebar > Search AI Avatar > Install ↓↓

  • Option 2: Install from the VS Code Marketplace: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=web-developer-hyper.ai-avatar ↓↓

How to Use the AI Avatar Chrome Version

Install from Chrome Web Store: ↓↓
https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/ai-avatar/afmcfaeaaojalninahhhjnonhmlmiidi

Special Thanks

  • My DEV Community friend and CCO (Chief Creative Officer) 🤣, @annavi11arrea1 collaborated with Catbot and AI Avatar in version 17, and keeps supporting me. Thank you very much!
  • My friend and CDO (Chief Design Officer)🤣, @rutenveil helped create the cool effects in version 15. and keeps supporting me. Thank you very much!
  • My DEV Community friend and CTO (Chief Technology Officer)🤣, @gramli helped update AI Avatar in version 2, and keeps supporting me. Thank you very much!
  • My DEV Community friend and CMO (Chief Marketing Officer)🤣, @itsugo. Our avatar collaboration project was the beginning of AI Avatar, and keeps supporting me. Thank you very much!
  • My colleague Maximum Blue helped make unique avatars in version, 6 and keeps supporting me. Thank you very much!

Version 29 Update

I'm already working on the version 29 update. More fun updates, so please stay tuned!

Outro

Ah! It's time for a security check, so I have to go now.💨 I would love to add more fun features and also use the latest AI in my next updates. I hope you enjoy the new updates to AI Avatar. Thank you for reading, and have a wonderful AI Avatar life!

Comments Welcome!

  • Do you have any ideas for more helpful security checks?
  • Do you have any ideas to make AI Avatar even more fun?
  • Do you have any ideas to add more AI features?
  • Do you have any ideas for making cool avatars and animations?
  • Do you have any ideas to improve the user experience?
  • Do you have any ideas for increasing the number of users of AI Avatar?

Any other comments are also welcome!

AI Avatar Security

In Japan, unauthorized access and sensitive data leaks caused by hackers have increased dramatically since September. I heard that personal data records exceeding twice Japan's population have now been leaked. This security situation does not seem to be happening only in Japan but also around the world. It’s quite horrifying. I wonder if this is partly due to the development of AI.

I have been using AI at work and for fun every day for more than a year, and I know how much smarter it has become in a short time. So this time, I decided to add a security support feature called AI Avatar Security to AI Avatar.

I am not a security expert, and I made it to learn about security. But I hope this will be helpful to others too. I also hope it will motivate others to learn more about security incidents.

There are three main features in AI Avatar Security.

  • Security Check
  • AI Review
  • Security News

Security Check

In Security Check, there are two types of checks. A library vulnerability check and a data leakage check. The library vulnerability check uses npm audit to check for the known vulnerabilities. It lets you know which libraries have vulnerabilities. The data leakage check uses Betterleaks (formerly Gitleaks) to detect exposed keys and passwords.

Security is not such a fun thing, but I added avatar animations based on the check results and tried to make it a little more fun and motivating.

NG Animation

If there are any security issues, a virus-like animation is played. It doesn’t mean the app is infected with a virus.🦠 I added the animation to make security checks more fun.

OK Animation

If there are no problems, a shining animation is played. Let’s feel relieved that there are no problems.

AI Review

I added an AI prompt for security checks to help prevent unauthorized access and sensitive data leakage. I also added an option to add tests for them.

类别 What AI checks
Unauthorized Access Login and authentication
Unauthorized Access 角色和权限
Unauthorized Access Data between users and teams
Unauthorized Access Private files and downloads
Sensitive Data Leakage Keys and passwords
Sensitive Data Leakage Private data in responses
Sensitive Data Leakage Logs and error messages
Sensitive Data Leakage Public files and storage

You can scan all eight at once, but scanning just one at a time seemed to provide a deeper analysis.

Security News

I added a security news checker. It uses two sources:

CIS (Center for Internet Security) for software vulnerabilities, and

NCSC (National Cyber Security Centre) for general security advice.

Please check the latest security news and update your security knowledge.

AWS Cleanup

By the way, I was also checking and improving my personal cybersecurity. I finally got off my butt and decided to clean up my AWS account. I was just stopping my services to avoid getting charged and wasn’t deleting them because I knew it would be so hard and take time.

Some of the services couldn’t be deleted all at once, and I needed to delete them one by one by entering their names. So I asked my AI to write code that could delete them all at once using CloudShell. First, I was deleting the services shown in CloudWatch logs, but soon I noticed that this didn’t cover all services. So next, I used Resource Explorer, enabled indexing in all regions, and checked which services I had used were still left. But default settings that didn’t need to be deleted also showed up. So I asked AI to scan and list only the services I had used. I finally deleted all the unnecessary services.

A few days later, I checked Cost Explorer and found that I had been charged a few dollars because deleting the services had triggered Config. I would have deleted the whole account if I had known it would be so hard and that I would even have to pay more.

However, I love using AWS because it is convenient and offers many services, so I would like to keep using it. But from now on, I will try to clean up regularly and avoid accumulating too many resources.
